# Independent audit of all four two-core minimum patterns

Read the complete source `candidate 50872e565640d12b`, Sections 1–3. **PASS**, with no correction identified.

The fixed-area radius set is compact inside a positive box: the PSD diagonal supplies the stated positive lower bound, and an adjacent core-product inequality supplies each finite upper bound. Closedness is therefore applied away from zero denominators. The exact PSD realization criterion makes this an attained optimization over actual feasible data, not a formal matrix relaxation.

The rigidity lemma correctly allows zero-excess edges. A strictly positive null vector forces every node slack to vanish and fixes the charge ratio on every positive edge. Positive-edge connected components have one-dimensional kernels; component scalings cancel from the reconstructed charges. Isolated zero-edge nodes introduce no undetermined sector vertex. At a zero edge the midpoint is an interior point of the actual core segment. All prescribed endpoints are straight joins, whereas exactly the positive-excess inserted vertices have positive turn. The support-preserving replacement argument therefore applies to every actual realizing body and forces equality with the unique polygon, rather than merely proving uniqueness within a chosen polygonal ansatz.

For all four patterns I checked both path components and both perturbations. A paired change preserves its zero core product exactly, decreases a non-target radius in one component, and increases a target radius in the other. If the decreased component were positive definite it would remain so locally; the increased component stays PSD by entrywise domination and its preserved Z signs. The other four strict excesses supply the required finite room. The target chord increases and one other chord decreases, so the normalized target inverse weight strictly decreases. In the two-plus-four patterns the free internal non-target radius perturbs only the four-node component and proves its singularity independently.

Thus both components are singular in every exactly-two-core pattern. Their positive null vectors concatenate to a globally positive null vector, and the rigidity lemma gives exactly four genuine vertices. The proof agrees with the independently derived double/double case in `candidate 91fb6de21f312a49`.

The stated limitation is essential and correctly retained: this classifies only a minimizing stratum with exactly two core sectors. It does not classify the additional-core strata, does not establish a triangle reduction, and does not preserve mixed-fiber compatibility.
